history.summary: A working Shiva temple inside the EME School campus at Fatehgunj, built in February 1966 by the Indian Army Corps of Electrical and Mechanical Engineers (EME) and run by the army establishment. It was planned and constructed under Brig A.F. Eugene, the EME School's first Commandant, who was himself a Christian. Its geodesic aluminium-sheet dome is deliberately secular: the kalasha represents Hinduism, the dome Islamic architecture, the tower Christianity, the golden tower-top Buddhism, the entrance Jainism, and the fire/havan kund Zoroastrianism. The main idol of Dakshinamurthy (Shiva as teacher) faces south, as he imparted jnana to the world; other features include a Ganesha idol and a silver arch engraved 'Om Namah Shivaya' (from Mahabalipuram), a replica Amarnath Shivalinga, and 100+ deity statues dated 6th-12th century displayed in the grounds. A Navgraha shrine, a scale replica of the main temple, was added in 2023 by Maj Gen Neeraj Varshney. Visitor-hours sources conflict: gujaratexpert says 9:30 AM-5:00 PM, closed Sundays; Wikipedia-sourced guides say 6:30 AM-8:30 PM daily - flagged (verify). Valid ID is required at the army gate and photography is strictly prohibited inside.

name: EME Temple (Dakshinamurthy Temple)
town_description: Vadodara (formerly Baroda) is the cultural capital of Gujarat on the Vishwamitri river, the historic seat of the Gaekwad rulers and home to Laxmi Vilas Palace, Maharaja Sayajirao University and Sayaji Baug.
